title: Finite ordinary embedded histories and admissibility relative to local values
statement: Let $A=(X\hookrightarrow P)$ be an embedded rational pair [def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution]. A raw history of length $n\geq0$ is a diagram of $n$ ordinary ambient blowups with specified ideal centers [def-nagata-global-blowup], their closed immersions into the successive embedded schemes, and specified scheme-theoretic strict transforms [def-nagata-strict-transform], retaining all structure maps, center ideals and their chronological order. Its initial schemes and inclusion are identified with $A$; no smoothness or reducedness of later stages is assumed. An extension identifies the entire previous diagrams and center ideals. A smooth comparison from a history on $A$ to one on $B$ lies over a cartesian smooth ambient map of initial pairs; it is cartesian over the initial schemes at every stage and commutes with all structure maps and inclusions. A monotone surjection of stage indices deletes precisely the stages whose pulled-back ambient center ideals are the unit ideal; every retained center is nonempty and its ideal is the extended ideal of the corresponding center. An intrinsic comparison over an isomorphism of the initial reduced schemes is a natural isomorphism of strict-transform diagrams preserving every earlier center ideal and its order, with no ambient identification. In particular earlier ideals remain recorded when intrinsic blowups are identities. For a totally ordered value set with least element $\bot$ and a simultaneous family $\nu_H:|X_H|\to V$ on raw histories, a maximum extension has as its new center the reduced full locus of a greatest value $m>\bot$. Admissible histories form the least class containing all empty histories and closed under these maximum extensions and smooth comparisons with deletion. Open restrictions are included as smooth ambient pullbacks. These are data and definitions, not an existence assertion.
